text.p: --BIRTHDAYS--
The English pioneer of the Catholic Church in Australia ARCHBISHOP JOHN POLDING was born in 1794.
Australian cricket captain WILIAM MURDOCH, who was the first Australian to carry his bat through an international match, was born in 1854. He died watching a Test match at the MCG.

Australian broadcasting pioneer WALTER CONDER was born in 1888. As manager of the ABC he was criticised for promoting sport and entertainment and was dismissed after allegations of financial mismanagement.

American rock musician and songwriter CHUCK BERRY was born in 1926. His hits included "Roll Over Beethoven" (1956), "School Days" (1957), "Sweet Little Sixteen" (1958), "Johnny B. Goode" (1958), "No Particular Place To Go" (1964) and his biggest hit "My Ding-A-Ling" (1972).
American actor GEORGE C. SCOTT, who won an Oscar for his lead role in "Patton", was born in 1927.
English/Australia actor, television compere and newsreader ROGER CLIMPSON was born in 1931.
Czech-born American tennis player MARTINA NAVRATILOVA was born in 1956. She won the Wimbledon women's singles title nine times and numerous other Grand Slam events.
--EVENTS--
1860 : British troops burned the Yuanmingyuan, the
imperial summer palace in Beijing, to the ground to avenge the deaths of captured British officers killed by the Chinese.
1873 : At a meeting in New York officials from Columbia,
Princeton, Rutgers and Yale universities formulated the rules of American football.
1910 : The trial of Dr HAWLEY HARVEY CRIPPEN began at the
Old Bailey. He was accused of poisoning his wife and the cutting her into small pieces which he buried in the cellar.
1922 : The British Broadcasting Company was formed to
begin broadcasting radio programmes in London. The company began transmissions a month later from Marconi House in London, under the management of JOHN REITH.
1931 : America's most prolific inventor THOMAS EDISON
died at the age of 84. Despite a lack of formal education EDISON went on to invent the phonograph, microphone and an electrical distribution system for lighting and power.
1947 : Two mail trains collided in Queensland killing
eight people.
1966 : The Queen granted a royal pardon to TIMOTHY EVANS,

who was convicted of the murder of his wife and child and hanged in 1950. The 25-year-old lorry driver was granted the pardon on the advice of the Home Secretary after a High Court judge found that EVANS was "probably innocent". The pardon was unprecedented in the history of British justice and followed a massive campaign by opponents of capital punishment.
1968 : JOHN LENNON and YOKO ONO were remanded on bail for
possession of cannabis following a police raid at their London flat.
1987 : The US attacked an Iranian oil rig in revenge for
strikes at its shipping by gunboats.
1989 : An earthquake measuring 7.1 on the Richter scale

rocked San Francisco for 15 seconds. Almost 70 lives were lost and billions of dollars in damage was caused in the Bay area. A section of the two-tier interstate 880 in Oakland collapsed crushing motorists driving on the lower deck.
1994 : Queen ELIZABETH II became the first British Royal
to ever visit Russia.
